skill.name: expense-view
skill.description: View and summarize expenses in the ledger.

attachment.anyPhrases: expense,expenses,spending,how much spent,total spending,transactions,for yesterday,for today,yesterday expenses,today expenses,yesterday transactions,today transactions,last expense,show expenses,recent transactions,recent expenses,categories of transactions,expense categories,show transactions

skill.view_intent:
0. If `expense-ledger-schema` is not already in the prompt or tool history, call `read_skill("expense-ledger-schema")` in the same turn as the `exec_sql` below (do not wait for a separate turn). For every view, list, search, or summary request, call `exec_sql` now. Use SELECT statements only; do not call `fetch_wise_transactions` and do not write data.
When the user asks for latest, recent, or last expenses with categories, call `exec_sql` with exactly this query:
```sql SELECT e.id, e.name, e.amount, e.paid_date, e.paid, c.name AS category_name FROM public.expense AS e LEFT JOIN public.category AS c ON e.category = c.id ORDER BY e.paid_date DESC, e.id DESC LIMIT 10; ```
- Include `LEFT JOIN public.category AS c ON e.category = c.id` whenever the user asks to show category names. - Use `ORDER BY e.paid_date DESC, e.id DESC` for latest/recent/last results. - Use literal `YYYY-MM-DD` date bounds supplied by system metadata for today or yesterday requests. - Select only the columns needed to answer the request; do not use `SELECT *`.
After the SQL result, immediately answer in plain text. If it is empty, say no matching expenses were found and offer to sync.
